P1.evidence: No setter and no setter notes read back. Rep skipped the four-part frame entirely and never asked for frame agreement — he opened with small talk then 'we have a limited amount of time. Let's dive straight into it. The floor is yours, Ryan. How can we potentially help you?' The open question was clean; the frame that should precede it was absent.

P2.evidence: Age (34), height/weight (5'9", 212), body fat, energy (5/10), desk-bound work, sleep and diet all asked. But health conditions own or hereditary were never asked — the ankle bone cyst, the smoking and the peptide use were all volunteered by the prospect, which scores as a miss. Training week and results from current training were never asked at all.

P3.evidence: Strongest phase by a distance. Rep drove surface to deep well: 'what do you feel like that's kept you from...what has it cost you' produced 'a balanced mental state' and 'lack of self-confidence affecting every aspect of life.' Ran the mirror exercise ('6th of May 2027...who do you want to see back'), ripple ('who else in your life is going to benefit'), and pushed through to partner and children. Reflected back cleanly at 00:40:37: 'you're not doing this to become jacked. You're doing this to have a cleaner and healthier mental state.' Never asked the specific 'something physical you want to do but can't' — golf came from the prospect.

P4.evidence: Rep never asked what he had tried before or what happened with it — the prior kettlebell class surfaced accidentally at 00:38:12 while discussing price. He did dig hard at root cause ('when you look at the blockers, the excuses, what do you feel like is the origin of that?') and got to comfort and fear of starting. The gap the prospect named was internal (comfort, fear), never structural — no structure, no progression, no accountability was never elicited, which left the pillars later doing unsupported work.

P5.evidence: Ran the two-year question extended to six ('you're 34 now...going to be 40 in six years, brother. What are the next six years look like?') and pushed through the prospect's deflection. Used the Usain Bolt / lion device to force a consequence image and got 'collapsing...a puddle of myself just blowing up and being immobile.' Settle-for and 'why not' were implied via 'that doesn't seem to be the path you want to go down' rather than asked directly. Line in the sand ran as 'are you actually ready to take that step, Ryan?'

P6.evidence: The commitment check was run out of order and incomplete. Rep asked 'are you ready to take the big step?' and got a yes at 00:20:22, but the belief question was only asked as a confidence rating AFTER the pillars were presented ('where would you place your confidence in us to help you get to where you want to be? Scale of 1-on-10?'), and the prospect never actually gave a number — he drifted into talking about Instagram videos. The 'if you had everything you needed, is there any reason you wouldn't go all in' question was never asked, so the price objection landed on an untested yes.

P11.evidence: A close was attempted but refused, so no payment, onboarding call, agreement email or welcome-email walkthrough was reachable. Trevor's onboarding call was described as a benefit during the pitch but never scheduled.

objection_plays.detail: Ran a large part of the financial picture — cash on hand ('three to five...thousand'), number of credit cards ('just the one'), available credit ('let's call it two grand'), savings ('$1,500'), credit score ('790'). Missed monthly surplus after bills and missed crypto/stocks/investments entirely. Critically, the isolation step never ran cleanly: he never asked 'finances aside, is there anything else keeping you from being 100% in', so he opened the wallet without first confirming the only blocker was money. He also skipped the scripted 'most clients pay upfront, but for some we break it up' framing and instead improvised a new three-month product at $4,000.

The prospect explicitly deferred on timing: 'we're getting right into golf season, and that's going to be very expensive. So I may have to follow up with you guys for winter.' None of the OD moves ran — no 'things never slow down', no 'when does it actually become the right time', no 'the longer you wait the harder this gets', which was unusually available here given a pending ankle surgery and a stated 10-year cycle. The rep went straight to money instead.
The prospect never asked for thinking time; he declined outright at the end.

Cheaper-substitute objection with no scripted play: 'that could definitely be a one-year membership at a nice country club...I could walk a course every day and maybe get the same level of movement for that same price', and at the close 'I'm going to continue learning off YouTube and saving the videos on Instagram and try it my way.' Objection C assumes the blocker is capacity to pay; here the prospect had priced an alternative he believed delivered comparable movement. This is the same gap already logged against the Badrane Hriouch call. Notably the rep had ammunition he never used — the prospect's own admission that saving Instagram videos is exactly what has failed him for ten years.

notes: Excellent phase 3 and 5 — this rep is genuinely strong at emotional depth and consequence framing. The call was lost in phases 2, 4 and 6: he never asked what had been tried, never let the prospect name a structural gap, and never got a hard pre-offer commitment, so the $6,000 landed on emotion alone against a prospect with $1,500 in savings. Coach the discipline of the commitment check before presenting, and stop solving affordability by inventing product.
